detail: No routine gate runs the UI test target, so a UI test can stay red indefinitely without anyone noticing. Measured: testBookshelfToReaderNavigation fails on main (50e990851) with 'com.Max0228.BooksBrowser crashed in <external symbol>', tests=1 passed=0 failed=1. Root cause is a fixture-id convention mismatch — BooksAndVocabUITests.swift:115 passes '-seedFixture:bookshelf:withBooksLibrary' (the camelCase CASE NAME) while BookshelfFixtureID's rawValue is snake_case 'with_books_library', so UITestFixtureSeed+Bookshelf.swift:7 BookshelfFixtureID(rawValue:) returns nil and failFixtureSeed preconditionFailures inside BooksAndVocabApp.init(). Dating: the bad call site is from 12166519f (2026-06-09); 2596c1595 'fail fast on UI fixture seed errors' is from 2026-06-14, FIVE DAYS LATER — it converted a silent mismatch into a hard crash, it did not cause it. FixtureDatasetUITests.swift:57 does it correctly via .bookshelf("with_books_library"), so a correct call site sat beside the broken one the whole time. The gap is the gate, not the bug: cutover routes UI tests only for branches that touch a UITest FILE, and the repo deliberately excludes the full UI suite as a block gate because of known flakiness — the combination leaves zero routine coverage.
plan: （1）新增 ops/ui_fixture_lint.sh：從 ios/BooksAndVocab/Support/Fixtures/Bookshelf/BookshelfFixtures.swift 的 `enum BookshelfFixtureID` 區塊抽出所有 `= "..."` rawValue，再掃 ios/BooksAndVocabUITests/ 內 `-seedFixture:bookshelf:<id>` 與 `.bookshelf("<id>")` 的字面值，不在清單者印檔名行號並 exit 1。（2）新增 ops/tests/test_ui_fixture_lint.sh：正例全過、注入 camelCase 假 id 必紅。（3）新增 ops/launchd/com.kg.uisweep.plist（比照 ops/launchd/com.kg.reconcile.plist）每日跑 `./ops/ios_ops.sh test --ui`，只做 advisory 不當 block gate。
resolution: Two separable fixes. (1) Type-safety: make the seed argument carry the rawValue rather than an interpolated enum case — UITestAppLaunch.swift:29 builds '-seedFixture:bookshelf:\(id)' from a stringly-typed id; taking BookshelfFixtureID and interpolating .rawValue makes the mismatch unrepresentable. bookshelf is currently the only domain resolving via Enum(rawValue:) (all others switch on hard strings), so this one site closes the class. (2) Coverage: run the UI target on a schedule (nightly / pre-sync) as an ADVISORY sweep with flaky-vs-real triage, rather than as a per-cutover block gate — the block-gate objection is about flakiness blocking every iOS cutover, which a non-blocking scheduled run does not incur. Fixed for this one test by feat/reader-liquid-glass d57c52add, which also repaired two other never-running UI tests; the gate gap remains after that lands.
